# tokens: # record — explicit record-shape constructor
# `refine Record [{a:Integer} {b:String} …]` builds a record type
# of single-pair maps. Each pair becomes one named field with a type
# constraint. Records are the explicit, named-shape counterpart to
# the implicit `{a:Integer}` literal — but the two have different
# semantics:
#   { a:Integer }                  — implicit shape, used for
#                                    structural `is` checks. The
#                                    parser flags the value as a
#                                    Node-family TYPE.
#   refine Record [ {a:Integer} ] — explicit record type value;
#                                    a stronger nominal-leaning form.
# In particular, `is` against an explicit `record [...]` is currently
# narrower than `is` against the implicit shape — the explicit form
# is intended primarily as a building block for `refine NAME record …`
# and downstream `make NAME` instantiation.
# This file documents:
#   1. Construction.
#   2. Rendering and typeof.
#   3. Naming via `def NAME (refine Record …)`.
#   4. Instantiation via `make NAME …`.
#   5. Structural conformance: which forms work, which return false.
#   6. Errors / malformed records.
# Runs against the production lang registry (test/go/langspec).
# 1. Construction
# The argument is a LIST of single-pair maps. Each pair contributes
# one field. The parser builds the inner `{k:Type}` literals as
# implicit-map shapes, which `record` consumes element-by-element.
# Note on rendering: a record value's underlying Data is a
# RecordTypeInfo, not a plain OrderedMap, so the spec runner's
# map-aware renderer falls through to v.String() — which emits
# fields comma-separated rather than space-separated.
refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]
note: one-field record

# tokens: refine Record [ { a:Integer } { b:String } ]
note: two-field record (comma-separated)

# tokens: refine Record [ { a:Integer } { b:String } { c:Boolean } ]
note: three-field record

# tokens: # Same-typed fields are fine — fields are by name not by type.
refine Record [ { x:Integer } { y:Integer } ]
# Field types may be any type literal, including subtypes.
refine Record [ { age:Number } ]
refine Record [ { tag:Atom } ]
# 2. typeof and is
# A record value's VType is Node/Map (records share the map vtype),
# so `typeof` reports `Map`. The richer 'this is a record'
# information lives in the value's Data subtype.
typeof (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ])
note: records are Map-typed under the hood

# tokens: (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) is List
note: a record is not a list

# tokens: # 3. Naming via `def NAME (refine Record …)`
# `def NAME (refine Record …)` binds NAME to the record type,
# making NAME usable as a type literal. The bound type is the same
# RecordType the body produced.
def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) R
note: the name denotes its minted node and renders as the name (§6); the field schema is the node's recorded content

# tokens: def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) typeof R
note: the RecordType's metatype is Map

# tokens: # Defining and re-querying.
def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } { b:String } ]) R
# 4. Instantiation via `make NAME …`
# `make NAME data` creates a value carrying the named record's shape.
# The result is a regular map-typed value (it round-trips through
# typeof as `Map`), but its underlying data carries the record's
# typed schema for downstream tools.
def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) make R { a:5 }
def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } { b:String } ]) make R { a:1 b:'x' }
def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) make R { a:5 } typeof
note: made record is a Map

# tokens: # A numeric field coerces between numeric leaves (Integer↔Float widening)
# but rejects a non-numeric source rather than laundering it into a number
# via stringify-then-reparse (WAT §V).
def R (refine Record [ { x:Float } ]) make R { x:3 }
note: Integer widens to a Float field

# tokens: def R (refine Record [ { x:Number } ]) make R { x:3 }
note: Integer satisfies a Number field

# tokens: def R (refine Record [ { x:Number } ]) make R { x:'1' }
note: a String is NOT laundered into a Number field

# tokens: def R (refine Record [ { x:Number } ]) make R { x:true }
note: a Boolean is NOT coerced into a Number field

# tokens: # 5. Structural conformance — implicit shape vs explicit record
# The implicit-shape form (`is { k:Type }`) does structural
# conformance and works as expected. The explicit record form
# returns false even on matching shapes — a documented asymmetry of
# the current design (records are intended as nominal types via
# `make NAME`, not as structural-conformance templates).
# Implicit shape — works structurally.
{ a:5 } is { a:Integer }
note: implicit-shape unification

# tokens: { a:'x' } is { a:Integer }
note: wrong type

# tokens: { a:5 b:'x' } is { a:Integer b:String }
note: multi-field implicit shape

# tokens: # Explicit record — narrower; plain maps do NOT satisfy it.
{ a:5 } is (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ])
note: a plain map is not a record

# tokens: def R (refine Record [ { a:Integer } ]) { a:5 } is R
note: even named, plain maps still fail

# tokens: # 6. Composition with def
# `def name body` captures the record TYPE as a value. A lowercase
# name is a value binding; a capitalised name would be a type
# binding (def is the universal binder — see TYPE-UNIFORM.10.md).
def sch (refine Record [ { x:Integer } { y:Integer } ]) sch
# 7. Errors / malformed records
refine Record [ ]
note: empty record list — must have at least one field

# tokens: refine Record { a:Integer }
note: argument must be a list, not a map

# tokens: refine Record [ 'not a map' ]
note: each element must be a pair (single-key map)

# tokens: # === D1 — record order-identity (design/FLEX-ATTRS.1.md §3.5.4) ===
# Field order is part of a record's identity: reordered bodies are
# DISTINCT, non-unifiable types (forced by positional-make soundness).
# Instances stay deq-equal by content — type identity is finer than value.
def R1 (refine Record [a:Integer b:Integer]) def R2 (refine Record [b:Integer a:Integer]) R1 unify R2
note: reordered field bodies do not unify

# tokens: def R2 (refine Record [b:Integer a:Integer]) make R2 [2 1]
note: positional make fills declared field order

# tokens: def R1 (refine Record [a:Integer b:Integer]) def R2 (refine Record [b:Integer a:Integer]) (make R1 [1 2]) deq (make R2 [2 1])
note: same-content instances stay deq-equal across order-variant types

# tokens: # === NUR068 — a record schema means the same thing as a fn RETURN ===
# A `refine Record` type declared as a fn's return keeps its field
# schema on the result (the same schema `make R` and a record-typed
# param carry), so field reads through constructor functions narrow
# and schema-breaking uses are declined. The negatives pin the compile failure
# side: a wrong-typed return, a field read fed to a map word, and a
# constructor result reaching a DIFFERENT record's param.
def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {name:'a' n:1}]] (mk) get 'name'
note: field read through a constructor fn

# tokens: def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {name:'a' n:1}]] (mk) get 'n'
note: second field, second type

# tokens: def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {name:'a' n:1}]] def use fn [[c:R] [String] [c get 'name']] use (mk)
note: constructor result into the SAME record's param dispatches

# tokens: def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def mk fn [[] [R] [17]] mk
expected: ERROR:mk: return value 1: expected Map, got Integer
note: declared record return still enforced

# tokens: def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {name:'a' n:1}]] keys ((mk) get 'name')
note: a schema-typed field read is not a map

# tokens: def R (refine Record [name:String n:Integer]) def S (refine Record [tag:Atom v:List]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {name:'a' n:1}]] def use fn [[s:S] [Atom] [s get 'tag']] use (mk)
note: a DIFFERENT record's param stays provably disjoint

# tokens: # === NUR069 (none axis) — a record field declared Any admits none ===
# Any is the top of the value domain: Any ∩ none = none. One reading
# at every boundary — make, a record-typed param, a declared record
# return, and the unify word itself — matching `is`, which always
# admitted none for Any.
def R (refine Record [x:Any]) make R {x:none}
note: make admits (as it always did)

# tokens: def R (refine Record [x:Any]) def f fn [[c:R] [Map] [c]] f (make R {x:none})
note: a record param admits the none-fielded instance

# tokens: def R (refine Record [x:Any]) def mk fn [[] [R] [make R {x:none}]] mk
note: a declared record return admits it too

# tokens: None unify Any
note: the unify word agrees: the intersection is none

# tokens: # ---- NUR069: a module fn's declared return is ENFORCED (2026-08-15) ----
# The CallBoru dispatch path used to TRIM to arity and ask nothing about
# type, so a module export returning the wrong shape passed silently on
# the interpreter while a compiled unit's RET raised — the same
# annotation enforced on one dispatch path and not the other. It now runs
# the frame path's own check (validateReturnTypesIn), so the two agree.
import module [def ok fn [[] [Integer] [1]] export "M" {ok: ok/v}] end M.ok
note: a conforming module-fn return passes, as before

# tokens: import module [def bad fn [[] [Integer] ['nope']] export "M" {bad: bad/v}] end M.bad
note: the violation the interpreter used to wave through (NUR069)

# tokens: import module [def bad2 fn [[] [String] [42]] export "M" {bad2: bad2/v}] end M.bad2
note: …in the other direction too

# tokens: import module [def free fn [[] [] ['anything']] export "M" {free: free/v}] end M.free
note: an UNDECLARED return keeps the historical flow-through — the residual IS the return
